subject: Air-gapped private deployment: registry signing + GitOps gating evidence
messages:
From: ACME Cloud <eng@acme-cloud.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: ops@sysops.io
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence for air-gapped deployment and registry signing

Hi Jonas / Kimberly,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Security team at ACME needs a compact evidence packet showing how Redwood will: 
- ensure artifacts deployed to their air-gapped clusters are provenance-verified (signed images)
- validate Terraform/Helm artifacts through the GitOps pipeline before on-prem promotion
- demonstrate CI gating for Ansible/Playbook runs in the restricted environment

Can you send a checklist or short runbook we can hand to our auditors? We also need to confirm whether signing is done by Redwood before shipping images to our disconnected registry or if ACME will pull signed artifacts and host them in their private registry.

Attaching the high-level SOC questions now; we may follow up with a formal questionnaire.

Thanks,
Jason Lee
Platform Security, ACME Cloud

[attachment: acme-soc-questions.pdf]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: eng@acme-cloud.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, priy a.natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence for air-gapped deployment and registry signing

Jason — thanks, this is exactly the kind of ask we expected. High-level answer up front: Redwood can provide signed artifacts plus a GitOps gating proofpack that documents CI checks, provenance assertions, and the transfer process to an air-gapped registry. Implementation is flexible: we can sign and hand off artifacts to ACME's registry, or provide the signing key material under HSM/KMS-controlled export policies to allow ACME to re-sign. We prefer signing in our build pipeline and publishing verifiable signatures; handoff to your registry is straightforward.

What I'll send now: a concise evidence checklist and the Terraform module manifest that shows module names, versions, and checksums (attached). Kimberly will add notes about CI gate jobs and Helm values to ensure nothing in values-level templates pulls external images at deploy time.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly to review the CI gating checklist and call out any extra gate jobs for airgap transfers.
2) Clarify whether ACME wants signed images only (sha + cosign) or a signed SBOM and image.
3) If ACME prefers local signing, we can provide a short runbook for signing artifacts inside their network using our recommended cosign/HSM pattern.

I attached the initial manifest and a CSV checklist that maps audit questions to artifacts.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

[attachments: priv-iac-evidence-checklist.csv, terraform-module-manifest.tf]

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, priya.natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence for air-gapped deployment and registry signing

Team — quick technical clarifications and an ask for ACME: I reviewed the manifest Jonas shared and sketched the CI gating/Ansible handoff we should provide as evidence. Key points below (I also attached a short playbook doc):

1) Artifact provenance and signing
   - We sign container images and the corresponding SBOMs using cosign (notary-style signatures) in our build cluster. Signatures are stored alongside images in OCI registries and exported as .sig files for transfer.
   - For air-gapped transfers, we produce a signed archive: image.tar + image.tar.sig + sbom.json + sbom.sig. The CSV checklist maps each artifact to the signing footprint.

2) GitOps gating pipeline (what auditors want)
   - Gate 1: Linting & SBOM generation (runner: isolated build pool)
   - Gate 2: Artifact signing & signature verification job (cosign verify step)
   - Gate 3: Policy checks (OPA/Rego enforcement on Helm values and Terraform variables)
   - Gate 4: Staging deployment in an isolated test cluster with smoke tests (no egress)

   Evidence items: pipeline logs, cosign public keys, SHA256 checksums, smoke-test results, and Git commit->artifact mapping. We should export these as a 'gitops-proofpack' tarball.

3) Terraform/Helm/Ansible modules to include in evidence
   - terraform-module-manifest.tf (attached) with module_version, checksum, and owner tag
   - helm-values-airgap.yaml to show disabled externalPull and imagePullSecrets mapping
   - Ansible playbook snippets (we'll include a separate playbook doc) showing 'force_local_registry: true' and idempotent checks

4) Registry transfer options (pick one):
   - Option A (preferred): Redwood hands off signed artifacts + proofs; ACME uploads to their offline registry and verifies signatures using our public key.
   - Option B: ACME provides a temporary HSM/KMS-backed signing environment in their network; Redwood provides CI jobs and signing automation to run inside ACME airgap.

ACME: which option do you prefer? If A, we need the contact for registry ingestion and the preferred manifest layout. If B, we'll prepare a 2-hour ops workshop and a bootstrap playbook (artifact-signing-playbook.md attached).

Minor: I added a Helm values file that toggles imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent and disables any chart hooks that pull from external endpoints. We'll include a checklist to reject charts with pre-install exec hooks.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Principal Infrastructure Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachments: helm-values-airgap.yaml, artifact-signing-playbook.md]

From: ops@sysops.io
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: eng@acme-cloud.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 14:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence for air-gapped deployment and registry signing

Thanks all — ACME prefers Option A for now (Redwood ships signed artifacts + proofpack). We've scheduled an ingestion window on Tue 2026-05-25 09:00 PT. Action items from our side and yours: 

- ACME ops (this thread): provide target registry credentials via the secure transfer channel and the expected manifest schema by Mon EOD.
- Redwood (Jonas/Kimberly): deliver the gitops-proofpack tarball (pipeline logs + cosign keys + checksums + smoke test report) and helm-values-airgap.yaml + terraform-module-manifest.tf before the ingestion window so we can validate on our staging importer.
- Marissa: can you own the evidence export and coordinate the drive folder with ACME security?

Jonas/Kimberly: please also confirm whether the cosign public key will be rotated post-transfer and the recommended verification commands for our auditors. We want the minimum viable packet to satisfy SOC reviewers but keep the door open for an on-site signing workshop later.

Appreciate the clear checklist in the CSV — it will help expedite the audit.

Cheers,
Sanjay Rao
SysOps Consulting — ACME engagement lead

[attachment: ingestion-window-instructions.txt]
